t: Shortest Distance After Road Addition Queries II
o: Start with a path 0→1→…→n−1 (distance n−1). After each added edge (u,v), report the shortest 0→n−1 distance. The guarantee that no two edges cross (no i<j<k<l pattern) makes the edge set laminar, which enables a simple backward-relaxation update instead of Dijkstra per query. Example 1: distances go 3, 2, 1.
k: Maintain dist[i] = shortest distance from i to n−1; initially dist[i] = n−1−i.
Adding edge (u,v): set dist[v] = min(dist[v], dist[u]+1), then sweep i from v−1 down to 0 relaxing dist[i] = min(dist[i], dist[i+1]+1).
The no-crossing guarantee ensures previously added edges lie entirely inside or outside [u,v], so one backward sweep fully propagates improvements.

a.i: Because edges never partially overlap, when (u,v) is added every older edge is nested within [u,v] or disjoint from it; hence recomputing dist right-to-left from v captures all new shortest paths in one linear pass.
s: For each query (u,v): dist[v] = min(dist[v], dist[u]+1).
For i = v−1 … 0: dist[i] = min(dist[i], dist[i+1]+1).
a.t: O(n·q) worst case (each sweep is O(v)), fast in practice given laminar edges

a.n: Approach 2: Ordered Set of Chain Segments
a.i: Model the graph as a set of 'jump segments': each existing shortcut covers an interval. A new edge (u,v) removes/decomposes all segments strictly inside (u,v) — possible without crossings — and inserts segment (u,v). The 0→n−1 distance equals n−1 minus total saved steps, tracked via a balanced BST / sorted list of segment endpoints.
s: Keep a sorted structure of active segments (u, v) with saving v−u−1.
On query (u,v): delete all segments fully inside (u,v), insert (u,v).
a.t: O(q log q + total removed segments) amortized

w: Approach 1 is the intended concise solution — lean on the no-crossing invariant explicitly when explaining why one backward pass suffices. Pitfall: initializing dist backwards (distance TO n−1, not from 0). Without the laminar guarantee you would need Dijkstra per query. Follow-up: version I of this problem has small n and permits per-query BFS.
